subject: Follow-up: Pricing & Latency tradeoffs — Redwood options
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Pricing & Latency tradeoffs — Redwood options

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo and the candid discussion earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same picture.

Call highlights (from our side):
- Workload: interactive search/chat embedded in your storefront — user queries -> 1–3 turns on average.
- Current token volume (est): 25M tokens/month today, forecast to 150M tokens/month within 6 months as you roll out to additional markets.
- Target unit economics: you called out a target of under $200 / 1M tokens as a goal to be sustainable with your margins.
- Latency SLO: p95 user-perceived latency target ~300ms for initial tokens (streaming preferred); end-to-end response < 1.5s for longer outputs.
- Budget: approximately $12k–$25k/month in the medium term (flexible if unit pricing improves with committed capacity).

Initial qualification / recommended approach:
1) Hosted (no-commit) vs Dedicated (reserved capacity):
   - For 25M -> 150M tokens/mo, the economics start to favor Dedicated if you can commit to a 3–12 month reservation — we can give substantive per-1M discounts at commitment levels that would bring you to your target $/1M band.
2) Latency vs cost levers:
   - Streaming + small batch sizes (1–4 requests) gives best user-perceived latency but reduces batching efficiency (higher $/token).
   - Larger batch sizes (16–64) and prefix/KV caching reduce $/token substantially but increase tail latency and could violate the 300ms p95 requirement for new queries.
   - Hybrid: deploy streaming on a low-latency tier for the top X% of traffic + a cost-optimized tier for background/async workloads.
3) SLO-driven pricing:
   - If you need guaranteed p95 latency (SLA), we recommend Dedicated SLO tier. We can build a pricing proposal that ties a portion of cost to a committed throughput SLA and preserves fallback to a lower-cost tier under burst.

Attachments: I included a simple pricing model CSV with a few scenarios (hosted/no-commit, 3mo reserved, 12mo reserved) and an SLO-options PDF with configuration tradeoffs.

Next steps / asks from you:
- Confirm the 25M -> 150M tokens/month growth assumption (or provide any revised numbers).
- Confirm whether you consider streaming required for the full traffic set or only for the first-response UX.
- If comfortable, indicate a target monthly commitment range (e.g., $10k/mo, $20k/mo, $50k/mo) so we can tune the reserved pricing scenario.

I copied Aditya (inference economics) and Dev (solution engineering) — they can put together a short proof-of-economics using a small sampling job and an SLO-backed dedicated quote.

Thanks — available for a 30-min sync this week if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
https://redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-model.csv (spreadsheet), SLO-options.pdf (PDF)
From: Alex Johnson <alex@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Pricing & Latency tradeoffs — Redwood options

Thanks Marissa — good recap, appreciate the docs. A few clarifications from our side:

- Tokens: 25M/month is accurate for the current pilot (A/B test on 10% of traffic). If the pilot goes well, we’ll roll to full traffic which is roughly 150M tokens/month as noted — timeline ~6 months.
- Budget: our finance lead gave a ballpark of $12k–$20k/mo for inference for the next 6–12 months, but that assumes we hit ~$80–150 / 1M tokens or lower.
- Unit target: ideally we want <$150 / 1M tokens. Anything north of $300 / 1M will be a tough sell without strong performance improvements.
- Latency: streaming for first-byte is important for the user experience on mobile. We’re open to having a hybrid approach (streaming for live sessions, batched for background re-rank jobs).

Can you run a quick calc: if we commit to a 12-month reserved pool that covers 100M tokens/month average, what ballpark $/1M could we expect on the model class similar to the one in the demo? Also: how much does enabling guaranteed p95 <300ms SLO typically move price?

If you can send a short comparison (hosted flexible vs reserved 3mo vs reserved 12mo, and SLO vs non-SLO pricing) that maps to our volumes, that’ll help the internal procurement conversation.

— Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product — Personalization
Acme Retail
alex@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Pricing & Latency tradeoffs — Redwood options

Alex — great questions. Short answers up front, then I’ll have Aditya/Dev follow with a calculator and a sample quote.

1) Ballpark pricing (model-class comparable to demo):
   - Hosted (no commit): ~$650–950 / 1M tokens (depends on throughput; streaming pushes toward higher end).
   - Reserved 3mo (medium commit): ~$320–480 / 1M tokens.
   - Reserved 12mo (larger commit, 100M+ avg): ~$140–260 / 1M tokens.
   - SLO impact (guaranteed p95 <300ms): ~15–35% premium on top of base reserved price depending on the tier and redundancy you require.

Notes: those ranges are illustrative — final numbers depend on exact model variant, quantization profile, and whether we use Dedicated GPU pools with autoscaling or a mixed reserved+burst strategy. Achieving <$150 / 1M is realistic at 12mo reserves and with model-quantization + caching enabled, especially if you can tolerate a hybrid routing policy for lower priority traffic.

2) Technical levers to hit targets:
   - Quantization and optimized kernels (Dev will run a short perf pass to quantify token/sec and latency).
   - KV/prefix caching for repeated session state (big wins if many repeated contexts).
   - Batch size tuning: aim for small batches (1–4) on the low-latency streaming pool and larger batches (16–32) on the cost-optimized pool.
   - Smart routing: route interactive sessions to low-latency tier; route async/rerank to cost tier.

3) Proposal flow:
   - Aditya will provide a spreadsheet mapping your volumes to the three pricing scenarios you asked for plus SLO uplift.
   - Dev can run a 24–48 hour sample job on our infra using a redacted slice of your prompts to measure real latency/token cost with streaming enabled.

If that sounds good, I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week with Aditya + Dev to walk the numbers and capture any procurement requirements.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Pricing & Latency tradeoffs — Redwood options

Alex — looping in the numbers as promised. Attached is a quick calc (same CSV Marissa referenced) with three scenarios. A few callouts:

- For 100M committed tokens/mo over 12 months, the illustrative blended price hits ~$160 / 1M with a Dedicated SLO tier (includes caching and quantization assumptions).
- If you want strict p95 <300ms across the board with 3x redundancy, you should expect +25–30% on the committed rate due to reserved low-latency capacity and redundancy.
- Streaming vs batch: we estimate streaming increases raw $/token by ~40–80% vs fully batched throughput at the same hardware; however, user-perceived latency improvements are often worth the delta for front-door traffic.

I’ll run a sample job as Dev suggested; can you share a redacted prompt set and a HIPAA/PII checklist if any of the data touches PII (we’ll redact client data for the perf pass)? Also flag any procurement/legal must-haves so we can bake them into the quote.
